groups.label: 11 · PUBLIC SOURCE PAGES / NO USER SESSION

nodes.label: Person using VeilX
nodes.detail: Starts a private conversation. Chooses protections, reviews detections and controls site permissions.

nodes.label: Extension shell
nodes.detail: WXT + Manifest V3, TypeScript, React and Tailwind. Coordinates local features and shows remote policy findings; the actual application is not built yet.

nodes.label: Protected prompt composer
nodes.detail: Raw names, addresses, email and phone are typed in an extension-origin side panel, outside the provider page. Only a reviewed redacted draft is copied to the chatbot.

nodes.label: Private restored answer
nodes.detail: Displays the readable answer inside extension UI. Original personal values never return to provider-owned DOM. Missing mappings stay visibly unresolved.

nodes.label: Toolbar popup
nodes.detail: Quick access to risk, current protection mode, session controls and opening the protected composer.

nodes.label: Local settings
nodes.detail: Standard/Strict preferences, auto-redact, per-site enable/pause, region-specific validators, clear-session action and privacy explanation.

nodes.label: Onboarding + permission guide
nodes.detail: Explain what stays local, what a domain-only audit reveals, cookie permissions, false negatives and the difference between protected and in-page composition.

nodes.label: Why this risk?
nodes.detail: Shows training, retention, human review, opt-out steps, checked-at and last-updated dates with evidence. Unknown facts remain unknown.

nodes.label: Live agent progress
nodes.detail: Shows sanitized server-relayed public-policy steps. In the real demo a verified TinyFish preview should make browsing visible; this graph performs no audit.

nodes.label: Active cookies / sessions section
nodes.detail: Dedicated local view of cookie domain, name/category, expiry and security flags. Values are not displayed, copied or sent to the server.

nodes.label: Optional site consent
nodes.detail: Request cookies + host access only when the person enables inspection for that site. Permission denial or revocation disables that feature honestly.

nodes.label: Privacy risk badge
nodes.detail: High, Medium or Low describes the documented training-risk rule, not a universal security certification. Loading, stale and failed states are visible.

nodes.label: Standard / Strict mode
nodes.detail: The policy result informs local detection sensitivity and the review gate. High or unknown risk selects Strict. Session secrets are blocked in every mode.

nodes.label: Typing + paste controller
nodes.detail: Handle input, paste, compositionstart/end and debounce. Do not run destructive rewrites during IME composition. Never dispatch raw drafts as custom page events.

nodes.label: Text spans + offset map
nodes.detail: Maintain source offsets and grapheme boundaries. Normalization for detection cannot shift highlight positions or silently change a user’s message.

nodes.label: Regex candidate engine
nodes.detail: Local bounded rules generate candidates for emails, phone numbers, cards, IDs and contextual addresses. Candidates still need validation.

nodes.label: Phone validator
nodes.detail: libphonenumber-js checks likely phone numbers using the selected region. Ambiguous local numbers require review; mobile and landline numbers share the PHONE category.

nodes.label: Card validator
nodes.detail: Apply length/prefix plausibility and Luhn checks. A checksum match does not prove a real card, so false positives remain reviewable.

nodes.label: ID / country rules
nodes.detail: Use explicit country/type-specific patterns and validators; avoid claiming universal government-ID coverage.

nodes.label: Address context rules
nodes.detail: Phase 1 recognizes explicitly labeled or structured address patterns and allows manual selection. Free-form addresses need local model support and review.

nodes.label: In-browser NER model
nodes.detail: Phase 2 uses transformers.js in a local worker for people and places. Model assets are packaged or explicitly downloaded; prompt text is never submitted for inference.

nodes.label: Cookie / token secret scanner
nodes.detail: Detect pasted Cookie headers, bearer credentials and session-like tokens locally. These are secrets, not ordinary restorable PII. Blocking is independent of risk mode.

nodes.label: Overlap + confidence resolver
nodes.detail: Resolve overlapping spans with deterministic priority: credential secrets first, validated exact patterns next, contextual NER afterward. Preserve offsets and require review for uncertainty.

nodes.label: Highlights + tooltips
nodes.detail: Accessible local highlights show category and replacement. Shadow DOM can isolate in-page styling but is not a privacy boundary; protected drafting stays in extension UI.

nodes.label: Detection review / manual mark
nodes.detail: Inspect candidates; remove false positives or manually mark a missed name/address. Auto-redact still offers review and never silently sends a secret.

nodes.label: Optional in-page convenience mode
nodes.detail: Provider scripts can observe raw text typed in their editor. Underlines or late redaction cannot undo that observation. This weaker mode must be disclosed.

nodes.label: Name → [PERSON_1]
nodes.detail: Example: Maya Chen becomes [PERSON_1]. In-browser NER provides general detection in phase 2; phase 1 supports manual marking and controlled demo fixtures.

nodes.label: Address → [ADDRESS_1]
nodes.detail: Example: 42 Example Lane becomes [ADDRESS_1]. Context patterns/manual selection first; expanded free-form coverage follows local NER.

nodes.label: Email → [EMAIL_1]
nodes.detail: Example: maya@example.com becomes [EMAIL_1]. Match complete email spans locally; keep punctuation outside the replacement.

nodes.label: Mobile → [PHONE_1]
nodes.detail: Example: +1 (202) 555-0148 becomes [PHONE_1]. Validate locally, normalize identity for stable repeats, preserve the original value in the private map.

nodes.label: Card → [CARD_1]
nodes.detail: Use local patterns plus Luhn. Store the original only in the temporary local map and keep it off audit requests and logs.

nodes.label: ID → [ID_1]
nodes.detail: Use the chosen jurisdiction’s detector. Highlight uncertainty rather than claiming every numeric string is an identity number.

nodes.label: Secret → [SESSION_1]
nodes.detail: A credential is replaced or removed before sending, and never restored in a reply. The temporary secret need not be retained in the placeholder map.

nodes.label: Entity registry + numbering
nodes.detail: Assign a stable type-specific counter per conversation. Repeated values share a placeholder; reserve/escape user-typed placeholder syntax to avoid accidental restoration collisions.

nodes.label: Temporary private mapping
nodes.detail: Conversation-scoped mapping from placeholder to original value. Only ordinary PII is restorable. Use memory or restricted chrome.storage.session, never synced or persistent storage.

nodes.label: Replace spans with placeholders
nodes.detail: Replace spans from the end of the string to preserve offsets. The exported draft contains placeholders in place of every reviewed original.

nodes.label: Auto-redact control
nodes.detail: Controls whether reviewed spans are replaced automatically. It does not weaken secret blocking or authorize automatic send.

nodes.label: Pre-send privacy gate
nodes.detail: Re-scan the exact outgoing draft. Block unresolved secrets, stale detection state and incomplete IME composition. A failed adapter never falls back to sending the raw draft.

nodes.label: Explicit clear + lifecycle cleanup
nodes.detail: Clear mappings on conversation close, explicit action and defined expiry. chrome.storage.session clears on browser restart/reload/extension disable, but does not replace application cleanup.

nodes.label: Missing / expired map state
nodes.detail: Leave unknown placeholders unchanged and explain the local session has expired. Never guess the original, retrieve it from the cloud or restore a different chat’s value.

nodes.label: Provider adapter registry
nodes.detail: Select only approved ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude adapters. An isolated-world content script accepts only redacted insertion commands from the extension.

nodes.label: ChatGPT rich-text adapter
nodes.detail: Find the approved editor and response region; update via provider-compatible input events; test paste, composition, regenerate and provider UI changes.

nodes.label: Gemini rich-text adapter
nodes.detail: Support its contenteditable editor and response region. Fail visibly if selectors or editor behavior change; do not send the unredacted fallback.

nodes.label: Claude rich-text adapter
nodes.detail: Support its rich-text editor, streaming messages and navigation. Keep chat identities isolated when the conversation changes.

nodes.label: Only the redacted prompt crosses
nodes.detail: The provider receives [PERSON_1], [ADDRESS_1], [EMAIL_1] and [PHONE_1]. It receives neither the private map nor original values through the protected path.

nodes.label: ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude
nodes.detail: Generates an answer using placeholder text. Normal first-party sign-in cookies can still authenticate the user; VeilX does not make the provider anonymous or hide its account identity.

nodes.label: Provider-owned page
nodes.detail: A trust boundary: page scripts may observe their own editor, DOM and account state. Protected original drafts and restored values stay outside this page.

nodes.label: Response MutationObserver
nodes.detail: Observe only the provider response area and copy provider-produced text to the extension channel. Tag/ignore own changes and avoid observer feedback loops.

nodes.label: Streaming token buffer
nodes.detail: Wait for complete placeholder tokens across streamed chunks. Preserve partial [PERSON_ fragments until their closing bracket arrives.

nodes.label: Exact placeholder parser
nodes.detail: Match complete tokens with the known type and number grammar. Unknown, malformed or user-escaped tokens remain literal text.

nodes.label: Conversation-scoped map lookup
nodes.detail: Resolve only tokens belonging to the current conversation and local session. A repeated token resolves to the same value; no cloud lookup exists.

nodes.label: Never restore credential tokens
nodes.detail: Reject restoration for SESSION, SECRET and credential types even if a model echoes them. Secret values must never reappear in provider output or its DOM.

nodes.label: Local plain-text restoration
nodes.detail: Reinsert approved original personal values with text nodes or React escaping. Show the restored result in extension-owned UI; do not execute model-supplied HTML.

nodes.label: Browser-native cookie store
nodes.detail: The browser owns actual cookies. A panel does not create an encrypted vault or move cookies to a separate protected container.

nodes.label: Permission-scoped cookie worker
nodes.detail: chrome.cookies + approved host permissions returns cookie objects, including values. Project the approved metadata immediately within the worker and never log or persist values.

nodes.label: Discard returned cookie values
nodes.detail: Drop raw values immediately after local metadata projection. No UI message, storage entry, audit request or TinyFish request contains them.

nodes.label: Metadata-only local objects
nodes.detail: Domain, path/name category, expiry/session status, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and partition metadata where available. No cookie value field in UI contracts.

nodes.label: Cookie flag checks + warnings
nodes.detail: Explain missing Secure/HttpOnly and SameSite context. Sites set their login flags; VeilX does not silently rewrite authentication cookies or guarantee no exfiltration.

nodes.label: Reviewed tracker rule set
nodes.detail: Explicitly reviewed known tracker endpoints. Broad blocking can break login; rules need site regression tests and clear versioning.

nodes.label: Chrome declarativeNetRequest
nodes.detail: Use matching rules to block known tracking routes without reading request bodies. This does not inspect arbitrary payloads or stop every leak.

nodes.label: Known tracker request blocked
nodes.detail: The browser blocks a matching request before it is sent. Unknown routes and permitted traffic are not automatically classified as leaks.

nodes.label: First-party login stays native
nodes.detail: Chrome attaches applicable cookies only under its domain/path/Secure/SameSite/partition rules. These normal authentication cookies can identify the account to its provider.

nodes.label: Per-site guard pause / resume
nodes.detail: Let the person pause optional request rules for a broken site. Secret scanning remains on, and the dashboard clearly shows paused enforcement.

nodes.label: Permission denied / revoked
nodes.detail: Remove associated rules and metadata where appropriate, stop inspection, show the feature as unavailable and keep local prompt protection running.

nodes.label: Approved chatbot navigation
nodes.detail: Notice supported-domain and conversation changes. Do not send visited URL paths, browsing history, prompts or cookie state to the backend.

nodes.label: Canonical domain allowlist
nodes.detail: Canonicalize approved ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude domains; reject arbitrary URLs. The exact supported domains must be verified when provider adapters are built.

nodes.label: Domain-only audit client
nodes.detail: Planned POST /api/audit body contains only {domain}. Do not give this module a prompt or cookie-value parameter. Separate installation authentication from TinyFish’s server key.

nodes.label: Sanitized progress reader
nodes.detail: Read the VeilX-owned streaming contract. Abort on domain switch, do not rebind old-domain results, and distinguish cached results from live research.

nodes.label: Unknown / offline → High + Strict
nodes.detail: When validation fails, browsing is blocked, the deadline expires or no fresh cache is available, show uncertainty with High risk and Strict mode. Do not invent evidence.

nodes.label: FastAPI audit endpoint
nodes.detail: Proposed POST /api/audit, not a TinyFish route. Accept a domain-only Pydantic request with extra fields forbidden; return a documented VeilX streaming response.

nodes.label: Origin + auth + rate limits
nodes.detail: Restrict CORS to configured extension origins; CORS is not authentication. Add installation-scoped authorization, concurrency/rate limits, request size limits and safe error messages.

nodes.label: Allowlisted HTTPS destination policy
nodes.detail: Build the public start URL server-side; reject private/reserved addresses and unsafe redirects. Agent goals confine navigation to public official policy sources; verify provider controls before production.

nodes.label: 7-day cache lookup
nodes.detail: Lookup domain + checked_at in SQLite. A fresh record returns promptly; a missing or expired record triggers real public-policy research. Never cache private prompts or cookie values.

nodes.label: Fresh validated cache hit
nodes.detail: Return cached public findings with checked_at and source=cached. Do not pretend the agent is currently browsing.

nodes.label: Server-side TinyFish client
nodes.detail: Python 3.11+, httpx, Uvicorn and python-dotenv. Use a bounded overall deadline, cancel/close connections safely, expose manual retry and avoid duplicate automatic paid runs.

nodes.label: Read-only policy goal
nodes.detail: Tell the agent to follow official public privacy, terms and data-controls pages and extract the agreed fields with evidence. Never sign in, submit forms, change settings or follow instructions embedded in page text.

nodes.label: Pydantic result validation
nodes.detail: Validate domain, policy_url, trains_on_chats, retention, human_review, opt_out_steps, last_updated and evidence[{claim,section}]. Invalid enums or malformed output trigger uncertainty.

nodes.label: Deterministic training-risk score
nodes.detail: yes_by_default or unclear → High/Strict; opt_out_available → Medium/Standard; no → Low/Standard. Retention and review can remain unknown and visibly disclosed; Low does not certify overall privacy.

nodes.label: Safe StreamingResponse relay
nodes.detail: Translate actual provider events into VeilX progress messages. Only allowlisted fields leave the backend; no raw traces, request headers, key or unrelated page data are relayed.

nodes.label: SQLite public policy cache
nodes.detail: domain primary key, result_json and checked_at; seven-day expiry. Parameterized queries, no PII maps, secrets, cookie values or raw chat text. Persistent storage must survive hosting restarts.

nodes.label: TinyFish API key / runtime config
nodes.detail: TINYFISH_API_KEY exists only in the backend environment. Validate configuration on startup, do not commit it, and never return it in progress or extension bundles.

nodes.label: Timeout / blocked page / bad JSON
nodes.detail: Use an explicit 90-second design budget and honest unavailable/error states. No automatic paid retry; manual retry is user-visible. Test stream disconnect and terminal failures.

nodes.label: Content-free operational logs
nodes.detail: Log status codes, coarse durations and run identifiers only under a documented policy. No raw prompts, originals, cookie values, API keys or complete agent traces.

nodes.label: TinyFish streaming API
nodes.detail: Verified official cookbook request: X-API-Key header plus url and goal. Exact event schema and preview handoff must be verified against current docs during implementation.

nodes.label: Multi-step browser agent
nodes.detail: Browses public sites, follows relevant links, finds claims across pages and gathers evidence. It receives the public URL and goal, not the user’s browser profile, prompt or cookies.

nodes.label: Provider progress stream
nodes.detail: Real progress, not timed decorative steps. Backend parses provider events defensively and maps allowed steps to its own contract.

nodes.label: Live browsing preview / recording
nodes.detail: Show an actual live run in the raw 2–3 minute demo. Preview permissions and returned URL handling are an integration check, not an invented API contract.

nodes.label: Structured policy finding
nodes.detail: Return the agreed policy fields and source claims. Unknown facts remain unclear/null. Agent output is untrusted until the backend validates it.

nodes.label: Official provider public website
nodes.detail: Starting point for public policy discovery. Pages can change, redirect or block the agent; static summaries do not replace evidence collection.

nodes.label: Privacy policy
nodes.detail: Evidence about training, retention, review and last-updated date. Claims should include a section reference and the relevant source URL.

nodes.label: Terms of service
nodes.detail: Read the applicable terms and linked policies. A plan or region may change the claim; do not silently generalize one page to every account tier.

nodes.label: Public data-controls instructions
nodes.detail: Find documented opt-out steps without entering the user’s account or using their authenticated cookies.

nodes.label: Source-linked evidence
nodes.detail: Evidence stays attached to the rating. Conflicting/blocked/unclear material is surfaced honestly; it does not become a low-risk guess.

nodes.label: Non-sensitive local preferences
nodes.detail: Only modes, site choices and UI preferences persist. No prompt text, PII map or cookie values; never use sync storage for private mappings.

nodes.label: Restricted transient extension state
nodes.detail: Restrict sensitive storage to trusted extension contexts. Browser-session lifetime plus explicit clear/expiry policies; no raw PII sent to content scripts.

nodes.label: Local model assets
nodes.detail: Packaged or user-approved model download; verify integrity/licensing, keep the NER worker local and report unavailable-model fallback.

nodes.label: Demo website playground
nodes.detail: Future local redaction playground using fictional samples and the same shared detection behavior. No real PII collection, analytics or external text submission.

nodes.label: Fictional examples + expected output
nodes.detail: Names, addresses, email, mobile, overlapping spans, unicode, repeated values, credential examples and unknown placeholders; no real accounts or cookie values.

nodes.label: Detection + map + restore tests
nodes.detail: Validate regex/validators, overlap priority, numbering, map expiry, unknown/partial placeholders and non-restoration of secrets.

nodes.label: Rich-text + streaming adapter tests
nodes.detail: Exercise each target: IME input, paste, keyboard send, button send, regeneration, conversation switch and UI selector failure.

nodes.label: Audit + fail-safe + cache tests
nodes.detail: Mock provider events: malformed JSON, cache hit/miss/expiry, timeout, blocked public pages, redirects, disconnects, rate limits and domain mismatch.

nodes.label: Cookie permission + sign-in tests
nodes.detail: Verify value-free messages/logs, permission denial/revocation, rule matching, site pause, first-party sign-in compatibility and no arbitrary payload-inspection claim.

nodes.label: Keyboard + reduced-motion checks
nodes.detail: Keyboard access, tooltips, visible focus, risk label not color alone, screen-reader progress and reduced motion.

nodes.label: Raw 2–3 minute live demo
nodes.detail: Unfamiliar chatbot → real public policy audit visible → High/Strict → fictional PII redaction → local restored answer. Cookie Guard is shown with honest capability limits.

nodes.label: Explicit opt-out authorization
nodes.detail: A future separate action to change provider training settings. Public policy auditing never authorizes account changes.

nodes.label: Training opt-out automation
nodes.detail: Design the authenticated execution boundary separately before implementation; prefer local settings navigation. Do not reuse or upload browser cookies to the public audit agent.

flows.label: Full system
flows.description: All proposed components and labeled connections. Zoom in or select a node to inspect its direct dependencies.

flows.label: PII → placeholders → AI
flows.description: Raw names, addresses, emails and mobile numbers stay in extension-owned UI and local temporary maps. Only placeholders reach the AI.

flows.label: AI reply → local originals
flows.description: Read placeholder replies, buffer streamed tokens, look up this conversation’s private map and restore personal values only in the extension panel.

flows.label: Active cookie protection
flows.description: Native cookies remain in Chrome. Optional local metadata inspection, pasted-secret blocking and known-tracker rules reduce specific risks; normal first-party login continues.

flows.label: TinyFish integration
flows.description: Only an approved domain enters the backend audit route. TinyFish researches public pages; validation, cache, safe progress and deterministic risk connect back to local protection.

flows.label: UI, storage + tests
flows.description: The proposed extension surfaces, non-sensitive preferences, temporary private state, local model assets, demo and acceptance checks.

flows.label: Stretch: opt-out agent
flows.description: Optional future authenticated settings changes require separate consent and an execution design that does not hand browser cookies to the public audit agent.
